response.task_summary: Predict whether a respondent has high blood pressure/hypertension using BRFSS survey features while favoring stable clinical and behavioral risk factors over domain-identifying variables.

ranking.rationale: Age is one of the strongest and most stable risk factors for hypertension across domains.
Diabetes is a clinically meaningful comorbidity strongly associated with hypertension.
Sex has a robust physiological relationship with blood pressure risk.
Recent physical activity is a broadly stable behavioral predictor of cardiovascular health.
The complementary physical inactivity indicator is also strongly relevant to hypertension risk.
Poverty captures socioeconomic stress and healthcare access effects that plausibly generalize.
Alcohol consumption per week is a direct behavioral risk factor for elevated blood pressure.
Lifetime smoking exposure is a meaningful cardiovascular risk marker.
The complementary lifetime non-smoker indicator helps encode stable smoking history.
Current daily smoking status is behaviorally relevant to hypertension and vascular risk.
Current non-smoking status helps distinguish present smoking behavior with plausible generalization.
Some-days smoking is still a meaningful cardiovascular behavior signal.
Vegetable consumption is a stable diet-quality proxy related to blood pressure.
Low vegetable consumption is likewise informative as an adverse diet indicator.
Fruit consumption is a generalizable diet-quality feature with plausible hypertension relevance.
Low fruit consumption complements diet-quality information relevant to blood pressure.
Binge drinking status captures harmful alcohol patterning beyond weekly totals.
The complementary binge-drinker indicator is similarly behaviorally relevant.
Foregone medical care due to cost reflects access barriers linked to unmanaged hypertension.
The complementary no-cost-barrier indicator still carries useful access information.
Race may reflect structural risk differences but is also vulnerable to shortcut learning, so moderate priority.
Unable-to-work status may proxy poor health burden relevant to hypertension.
Retired status often tracks older age and health status, though partly redundant with age.
Homemaker status may weakly reflect lifestyle and socioeconomic patterns related to health.
Employment for wages provides some socioeconomic and routine-related signal but is less direct.
Self-employment may weakly capture socioeconomic and stress-related differences.
Long-term unemployment may proxy chronic stress and poorer health.
Short-term unemployment may carry weaker but still plausible socioeconomic signal.
Student status is mostly age-related and less directly tied to hypertension.
Skin cancer history may weakly proxy age and healthcare contact but is not a core hypertension factor.
Absence of skin cancer offers limited complementary health-history information.
Other cancer history may weakly reflect age and comorbidity burden.
No other cancer is only weakly informative as a complementary health-history marker.
Missingness on physical activity may encode survey process more than health, but could still correlate with risk.
Missing binge-drinking status is mostly a response artifact with limited stable value.
Missing fruit-consumption status is mainly a survey-response artifact.
Missing vegetable-consumption status is mostly process noise rather than semantic risk.
Missing medical-cost response may weakly reflect disengagement but is not semantically robust.
Missing lifetime smoking history is mostly a data artifact.
Don't-know smoking response is less semantically meaningful than substantive smoking categories.
Refused smoking response is primarily a response-style artifact.
Missing employment status is mostly survey-process information.
Missing skin-cancer status is weak and likely non-transportable.
Missing other-cancer status is similarly weak and process-driven.
Not-asked smoking status is heavily tied to questionnaire flow rather than underlying hypertension risk.
Survey year can encode temporal shifts and benchmark split structure rather than stable biology.
State identity is a strong domain indicator and should be heavily penalized for OOD generalization.
